de: campus district energy: steam at 205 °C, 590 MW; chilled water at 5 °C, 145 MW; 80 buildings (CEEDC district-energy inventory, reported 2017). It also serves customers in the Greater Campus Area; its fuel was 136,705 t CO2e in 2023–24, and the University is weighing a conversion to low-temperature hot water (Operational GHG Emissions Reduction Plan, 2025). A lower-temperature network would need less lift from server heat. Its own plan cuts campus energy intensity 15% by 2030, partly through heat recovery inside its buildings, so its demand for outside heat would fall (Envision Energy Reduction Master Plan, 2021)
